official.deadline_note: MEXT publishes no single deadline. The deadline for submission of application documents varies according to each Japanese diplomatic mission, and applicants must confirm the deadline at the website of the mission in their country of nationality. For the 2027 intake, the call for applications opened around mid-April 2026 and First Screening was conducted from early May to late July 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake - arrival in Japan April 2027 term or September/October 2027 term; embassy recommendation recruitment April-May 2026, final results notified January to early March 2027
official.status_note: For arrival in 2027, application documents were submitted to Japanese diplomatic missions around April-May 2026 with First Screening from early May to late July 2026; provisional acceptance requests closed on 1 September 2026 and Placement Preference Forms were due mid-September to early October 2026. As of the 2026-10-10 verification the cycle is between First and Second Screening, with MEXT second screening and university placement from November 2026 and results notified January to early March 2027. The official 2027 page still publishes the full guidelines and FY2027 forms; recruitment for the next intake opens around April of the previous year.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Education fees: fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities are waivered. The entrance examination fee, however, will be borne by the grantees if they cannot proceed to the master's or doctoral course or cannot be admitted to the university.
benefits: 143,000 yen per month for students receiving the preparatory education and non-regular students
144,000 yen per month for regular students enrolled in master's or professional degree courses
145,000 yen per month for regular students enrolled in doctoral courses
A supplemental regional allowance of 2,000 yen or 3,000 yen per month for grantees studying or conducting research in specially designated regions
Fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities are waivered

Economy-class airline ticket provided for transportation to Japan during the specified arrival period and, on application, transportation from Japan for grantees graduating and returning by the end of the final month of the scholarship period
eligibility: Applicants must have the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; an applicant who has Japanese nationality at the time of application is not eligible (dual nationals residing outside Japan may apply if they choose the other nationality and relinquish Japanese nationality by arrival in Japan)

Applicants, in principle, must have been born on or after April 2, 1992 (under 35 years of age; exceptions are limited to country circumstances such as military service obligation or war-related loss of educational opportunities)

Applicants must satisfy one of the published academic-background conditions for admission to a master's or doctoral course at a Japanese graduate school, e.g. completion of 16 years of school education, completion of a three-year-or-longer bachelor-equivalent programme, an overseas degree equivalent to a master's for the doctoral second phase, or 18 years of schooling for doctoral courses in medicine, dentistry, veterinary science and certain pharmaceutical fields
Applicants must be willing to learn Japanese, be interested in Japan, and have the ability to conduct research and adapt to living in Japan
Applicants must be able to arrive in Japan in the April 2027 term (in principle between 1 and 7 April 2027) or the October 2027 term, and must newly obtain a Student visa
Applicants must submit a health certificate in the prescribed format signed by a physician attesting no physical or mental conditions hindering study in Japan
requirements: Submit the complete document set to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of the applicant's nationality by the designated deadline; submitted documents are not returned and must not be sent directly to MEXT in Japan

Use the FY2027 forms for the Application Form, Placement Preference Application Form, Field of Study and Research Plan and Certificate of Health, and write the document numbers 1 to 11 in the upper right-hand corner of the first page of all documents
Documents must be written in Japanese or English, or a Japanese or English translation must be attached

Up to three universities may be filled in the Placement Preference Application Form, at most two letters of provisional acceptance may be obtained, and at most two universities may be contacted at the same time

Contact with universities to request issuance of a letter of provisional acceptance made on Wednesday, September 2, 2026 or after is not permitted; applicants should first contact the division of international student affairs (not the intended supervisor), and only letters in the MEXT-specified format are accepted

First Screening includes written examinations of language proficiency in Japanese and English taken by all applicants, with the English proficiency test possibly exempted for countries where English is the official language
documents: Application Form (FY2027 form) with a 4.5 x 3.5 cm upper-body, full-faced photograph taken within six months, applicant's name and nationality written on the back
Placement Preference Application Form (FY2027 form), listing up to three universities
Field of Study and Research Plan (FY2027 form) describing the applicant's past and present field of study and the research theme and plan in Japan

Academic transcript for all academic years of university attended, issued by the university or the applicant's national government and showing the grade scale, plus certification of graduation or degree certificate (a certificate of prospective graduation if the applicant has not yet graduated)

Recommendation letter from the president/dean or the academic advisor at the current or last university attended (free format, sample available) and a medical certificate on the FY2027 Certificate of Health form completed by a physician

If applicable: abstracts of theses (graduation thesis and presented papers acceptable), certificate of Japanese or English language proficiency in 3 copies issued no earlier than two years before application, recommendation letter from the present employer, and photographs of the applicant's own works of art or a digitally recorded media of musical performance for fine arts or music applicants
selection_criteria: Examination of submitted application documents: academic achievement at the university last attended equal to or exceeding a certain level, and a research plan stated in a detailed and concrete manner
Written examination of language proficiency: Japanese and English proficiency adequate for research at a Japanese university

Interview: a clear sense of purpose relating to study in Japan, information gathered about Japanese universities, and sufficient Japanese or English ability to communicate with the academic advisor in Japan (considerable Japanese proficiency for subjects requiring advanced Japanese)

Second Screening by MEXT based on the First Screening results, with grantees selected once placement at a university is decided; a letter of provisional acceptance greatly influences final results and applicants may be rejected without one
An application may be rejected if it arouses weapons proliferation concerns, including those over weapons of mass destruction and related items
coverage: Monthly scholarship of 143,000 yen (preparatory education and non-regular students), 144,000 yen (regular master's and professional degree courses) or 145,000 yen (regular doctoral courses), with a 2,000 or 3,000 yen monthly supplemental regional allowance in specially designated regions
Waiver of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees at the university
Economy-class round-trip airfare between the grantee's residence and Japan within the specified arrival and return periods
Up to six months of preparatory education in the Japanese language before placement at the university for those who require it
application_method: Read the Application Guidelines for Research Students (FY2027) and follow the instructions in full

Download and complete the FY2027 Application Form, Placement Preference Application Form, Field of Study and Research Plan and Certificate of Health, and assemble transcripts, graduation certification, recommendation letter and any conditional documents
Submit the document packet to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the country of your nationality by the mission's designated deadline; do not send documents directly to MEXT in Japan

After passing the First Screening, request letters of provisional acceptance directly from up to two universities at a time (sending the Passing Certificate of the First Screening and the stamped copy set by e-mail), then submit the final Placement Preference Application Form to the Japanese diplomatic mission
official.application_route: Embassy recommendation: submit the FY2027 document packet to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality by its published deadline, then complete the first screening (documents, written Japanese and English examinations, interview) at that mission.
official.study_mode: Full-time, as regular students (enrolled in a degree course) or non-regular students conducting research
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must have the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan and apply through the Japanese diplomatic mission of that nationality; applicants with Japanese nationality at the time of application are not eligible, except dual nationals residing outside Japan who choose the other nationality and relinquish Japanese nationality by arrival in Japan
official.international_eligibility: The scholarship is for international students only; eligibility depends on nationality of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan rather than on residence, and applications are handled by the Japanese diplomatic mission of the applicant's nationality
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants should apply for the field of study they majored in at university or its related fields, and fields of study may be restricted to particular fields specified by the Japanese diplomatic mission in the applicant's country; traditional entertainment arts such as Kabuki and classical Japanese dance, and subjects requiring practical training at factories or companies, are excluded, and students of medicine, dentistry or welfare science cannot engage in clinical training until licensed
official.research_requirement: The Field of Study and Research Plan (FY2027 form) must describe the applicant's past and present field of study and the research theme and plan in Japan and serves as an important reference for university placement; document screening requires the research plan to be stated in a detailed and concrete manner
official.duration: Non-regular students: from April 2027 until the end of March 2029 (or from September/October 2027 until the end of March 2029 for October-term arrivals), with the first 6-month period devoted to Japanese-language preparatory education for those who require it. Regular students in master's, doctoral or professional graduate courses: the standard period of study for the course (master's two years, doctoral three years, professional degree two years, three years for graduate law schools), with up to 6 months of preparatory education added where the accepting university deems it necessary. Extension of the scholarship period for advanced study is possible with MEXT approval.
official.description: The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) of Japan offers scholarships to international students who wish to study in graduate courses at Japanese universities as Research Students (either regular students or non-regular students) under the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship Program. The 2027 embassy-recommendation round funds arrivals in Japan in April 2027 or September/October 2027 and pays a monthly scholarship depending on the course enrolled in, waives entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees, and provides round-trip airfare.
official.region: Global - applicants apply through the Japanese diplomatic mission in their country of nationality
official.program_type: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship - Research Students, Embassy Recommendation

not_confirmed: deadline_central (MEXT publishes no single deadline; each Japanese diplomatic mission sets its own submission deadline)
english_requirement as a score (no minimum IELTS/TOEFL score or MOI rule is published; selection uses written Japanese and English examinations and an interview instead, so the field is null)
list of specially designated regions eligible for the 2,000-3,000 yen supplemental regional allowance (not published on these pages)
per-country field-of-study restrictions (set individually by each Japanese diplomatic mission)
verification.notes: Monthly allowance, tuition waiver and travel benefits were taken from Section 6 of the FY2027 Application Guidelines for Research Students on the official Study in Japan (JASSO/MEXT) site and cross-checked against the MEXT Scholarship overview page, which publishes 143,000-145,000 yen per month, tuition exempted and round-trip airfare; process dates come from the guidelines' application process chart and the embassy recommendation page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is Japan's flagship government scholarship for graduate-level research, and under the embassy-recommendation route you apply to the Japanese embassy in your own country rather than to any university. The package is a monthly living stipend of 143,000-145,000 yen depending on your student status, waived tuition and admission fees, and economy-class round-trip airfare. The binding constraint is placement: you may name only three preferred universities, a letter of provisional acceptance strongly influences whether you are selected at all, and every milestone date after the written exam is set by the embassy handling your country rather than by MEXT centrally.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates and early-career researchers under 35 with a 16-year schooling background or equivalent who want fully funded master's or PhD research in Japan and are willing to learn Japanese.
application_readiness_checklist: Find the Japanese embassy or consulate-general page for your country and record its exact document deadline, since it is set per mission and can fall well before the end of May

Download the FY2027 forms (Application, Placement Preference, Field of Study and Research Plan, Certificate of Health) and keep the document numbers 1 to 11 consistent on the first page of every document

Collect transcripts covering every academic year with the grade scale shown, plus a graduation certificate or certificate of prospective graduation, and start certified Japanese or English translations early
Request the free-format recommendation letter from your dean or academic advisor now, and book a physician appointment for the MEXT-format Certificate of Health
Prepare a 4.5 x 3.5 cm photograph taken within the last six months with your name and nationality on the back
Draft a shortlist of no more than three Japanese universities and a concrete research plan before the First Screening, so that provisional-acceptance emails can go out immediately after results
common_rejection_risks: Failing to obtain any letter of provisional acceptance, since MEXT warns applicants may be rejected without one
A vague or generic research plan, when document screening explicitly requires a detailed and concrete plan

Breaching the contact rules: contacting more than two universities at once, obtaining more than two acceptance letters, contacting the intended supervisor instead of the international student affairs division, or making contact on or after 2 September 2026
Missing the embassy's own deadline because a central date was assumed, or sending documents directly to MEXT in Japan
Being already enrolled, or planning to enrol, in a Japanese institution as a privately financed student, or applying simultaneously to another MEXT programme
Completing a previous MEXT scholarship within the past three years, or entering Japan without a newly obtained Student visa, which suspends payment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation in university residence halls or private apartments (sometimes payable in advance before arrival), domestic travel from home to the departure airport, airport taxes and usage fees, travel insurance, carry-on or unaccompanied baggage, and National Health Insurance premiums. MEXT itself recommends bringing approximately US$2,000 because the first stipend installment is paid only one to one-and-a-half months after arrival.
document_audit: Transcripts must cover every academic year and show the grade scale; a degree certificate or a class-ranking letter cannot substitute for transcripts
If you have not yet graduated, a certificate of prospective graduation is required instead of a graduation certificate, and the final certificate must reach the mission by enrolment
The medical certificate must be on the FY2027 Certificate of Health form completed by a professional medical doctor; a generic doctor's letter does not meet the requirement
Any change in health circumstances after submission must be reported promptly to the mission, so keep the examining physician's details
Language certificates are optional but, if submitted, must be issued within two years of application and provided in 3 copies; print the page showing your name, level and score
Do not send irreplaceable originals: submitted documents are not returned and bound documents may be dismantled during review, so use attested copies
alerts: The only real deadline is your own embassy's; the central page states only that recruitment runs April-May of the previous year and that screening dates vary by mission

Provisional-acceptance requests made on or after 2 September 2026 are not permitted, and universities generally need about a month to issue a letter, so start the summer before results with emails ready
Fields of study can be restricted by your embassy and vary by country, and traditional entertainment arts or company-based practical training are not eligible fields

If your preferences mix private and national universities, national universities are prioritised regardless of your stated order, and applicants without any acceptance letter are restricted to the October term
Monthly amounts are reviewed against the national budget each fiscal year and the 2,000-3,000 yen regional supplement applies only in specially designated regions

A positive infectious-disease test, including tuberculosis, at the medical exam must be fully treated before arrival is approved, and grantees must open a Japan Post Bank account because stipends are paid only there
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Paper packet to your Japanese embassy or consulate by its own deadline, then document review plus written Japanese and English examinations and interview at the mission, then e-mail a Passing Certificate and stamped copy set to up to two universities at a time for provisional acceptance, then the Placement Preference Application Form back to the mission, and finally MEXT second screening and placement with results via the mission from January to early March 2027.
